h1: How to choose an unvented-cylinder engineer
title: How to choose an unvented-cylinder engineer | G3 Hot-Water Knowledge
description: Understand how to choose an unvented-cylinder engineer with clear model-aware information and practical questions for your cylinder engineer.
answer: Choose someone competent for the actual cylinder and work, with evidence of relevant training, clear scope and a explained notification route where applicable.

sections.heading: The key distinction
paragraphs: Ask who will attend, which product family they will work on and what evidence supports the required competence. A supplier logo, broad experience statement or copied badge is not a substitute for the individual record. Electrical or connected gas work may require additional qualifications.

sections.heading: Apply the information to the installed system
paragraphs: The quotation should state the task, limitations and proposed handover. For installation, clarify commissioning and any Building Regulations notification. For repairs, ask what will be tested and which record will describe the completed work.

sections.heading: A practical next question
paragraphs: Gather the full model, heating method, recent symptoms and available paperwork. Discuss the scope with a person competent for the actual work. Technical information here supports that conversation and is not a substitute for manufacturer instructions or individual system assessment.

faqs.question: What evidence should I ask for before unvented-cylinder installation?
faqs.answer: Ask for relevant competence, the attending installer, product experience, commissioning scope and the proposed Building Regulations notification route for the job.
